### Executive Summary
- Multiple **actively exploited / high-impact vulnerabilities** surfaced (notably **Wing FTP Server** per CISA and a **critical unauth root RCE in telnetd CVE-2026-32746**); verify exposure and block/patch fast.
- **Social engineering + remote assistance abuse** is trending again (Teams “support call” → **Quick Assist compromise**); tighten controls and hunt for suspicious remote-control activity.
- **Ransomware + wiper tradecraft is shifting toward stealth + data theft** (LeakNet “ClickFix” + in-memory Deno loader; Medusa/Warlock activity; Iran-linked wiper reporting) → prioritize identity telemetry, lateral movement, and destructive-action detections.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) CISA: Wing FTP Server vulnerability actively exploited (KEV-style operational urgency)**
- What happened: CISA and multiple outlets flagged a **Wing FTP Server CVE** as **exploited in the wild**.
- Why it matters operationally: Internet-facing file transfer services are common footholds leading to **credential theft, webshells, and ransomware staging**.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Confirm if any Wing FTP is deployed/exposed** (asset inventory + external scan); **patch/mitigate now or isolate behind VPN**, add temporary **WAF/IPS virtual patching** and block inbound from untrusted networks.

**2) Critical telnetd unauthenticated root RCE (CVE-2026-32746) on port 23**
- What happened: Reporting indicates an **unpatched telnetd flaw** enabling **unauthenticated root RCE** over **TCP/23** with public PoC discussion.
- Why it matters operationally: Telnetd exposure is high-risk and often overlooked on **embedded/legacy Linux/Unix**; rapid opportunistic scanning is likely.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Search perimeter rules and flow logs for any TCP/23 exposure**; **block TCP/23 at the edge immediately** (deny inbound, alert on attempted connections), and task IT to **remove/disable telnetd** where present.

**3) Vishing → Microsoft Teams “support call” leading to Quick Assist compromise**
- What happened: New campaign reported where attackers use **Teams-based vishing** to convince users to grant control via **Windows Quick Assist**.
- Why it matters operationally: This bypasses many email controls and yields **interactive access** (hands-on-keyboard), enabling rapid **credential access and payload deployment**.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Hunt for Quick Assist executions and remote-control sessions** on endpoints; if feasible, **restrict/disable Quick Assist** via policy for non-helpdesk users and reinforce user guidance: “no unsolicited support sessions.”

**4) Ransomware tradecraft update: LeakNet/Warlock/Medusa + “ClickFix” and in-memory loaders**
- What happened: Reports highlight ransomware operators using **ClickFix via compromised sites**, **in-memory Deno runtime loaders**, and expanded **post-exploitation** (Warlock); Medusa claims new victims.
- Why it matters operationally: Tactics reduce file-on-disk artifacts and accelerate **credential theft + lateral movement**, increasing risk of **data exfiltration** and disruptive encryption in financial environments.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Prioritize detections for in-memory/script runtimes (Deno/Node/PowerShell)** and unusual archive/exfil tools; **raise triage priority** for alerts involving helpdesk tools, LOLBins, and suspicious web-driven “fix/captcha/update” user flows.

**5) Supply-chain risk: GlassWorm targeting code ecosystems (npm/React Native + Python repos via stolen GitHub tokens)**
- What happened: “GlassWorm” is reported evolving into **credential-stealing packages** (npm/React Native) and **Python repo targeting** using **stolen GitHub tokens**.
- Why it matters operationally: Developer workstations and CI/CD tokens are high-value in financial services; compromise can lead to **internal code tampering, secret theft, and downstream deployment risk**.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Monitor for anomalous GitHub/token usage** (new IPs, unusual PAT scopes, mass clone/publish); ask AppSec/DevOps to **pin deps, scan SBOM/artifacts**, rotate exposed tokens, and enforce **MFA + least-privilege** on org repos.

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **Internet edge / scanning:** Monitor firewall/NDR for **inbound TCP/23** attempts and any unexpected telnet traffic (ATT&CK **T1190** Exploit Public-Facing App / service exposure); alert on spikes and geo anomalies.
- **Wing FTP exposure & compromise signals:** From **reverse proxy/WAF, IDS/IPS, and server logs**, hunt for abnormal requests, new admin sessions, file uploads/executions, or creation of new accounts (T1190, **T1505** Server-side component).
- **Quick Assist / remote control abuse:** From **EDR + Windows Security logs**, alert on **QuickAssist.exe** launches, remote control session start, unusual parent processes, and execution shortly after Teams calls (ATT&CK **T1219** Remote Access Tools).
- **Teams vishing lead-in:** From **M365 audit logs / Defender for Office / Teams logs**, hunt for unusual external contacts initiating “support” chats/calls, repeated contact attempts, or links to “fix/verify” pages (ATT&CK **T1566** Phishing—vishing-adjacent).
- **In-memory/script runtime staging (LeakNet-style):** From **EDR telemetry**, hunt for **deno.exe / node.exe / powershell.exe** with suspicious network beacons, base64/encoded command lines, or child processes spawning credential tools (ATT&CK **T1059**, **T1027**).
- **Credential access + lateral movement surge (ransomware post-ex):** From **AD/IdP, Windows logon, and PAM**, alert on abnormal **Kerberos/NTLM authentication patterns**, new service creation, remote exec (WMI/PSRemoting), and rapid privilege changes (ATT&CK **T1078**, **T1021**).
- **GitHub token/repo abuse:** From **GitHub Enterprise audit (if used), CASB, and proxy logs**, alert on PAT use from new ASN/IP, bulk repo downloads, unusual package publish actions, and secrets access (ATT&CK **T1552** Unsecured Credentials).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch/hardening backlog triage:** Validate exposure and remediation plans for **FortiClient SQL injection** reporting and the **Snap local privilege escalation (CVE-2026-3888)** on Linux fleets; prioritize systems with developer/admin access.
- **Browser/device security:** Apple “Background Security Improvements” addressing a **WebKit flaw**—ensure mobile fleet update compliance; also track reports of **Chrome 0-days** (details unclear in the feed—assume rapid patch cadence required).
- **Sentinel operational change:** Microsoft Sentinel **HTTP Data Collector API transition**—confirm ingestion pipelines, update connectors, and set monitoring so logging doesn’t silently drop (treat as detection-coverage risk).
- **Software supply-chain controls:** Expand dependency governance (lockfiles, private registries, allowlists) to reduce exposure to **trojanized npm/Packagist themes**; require automated secret scanning and token rotation playbooks.
- **Ransomware readiness:** Given trend toward **data theft over pure encryption**, review egress controls (CASB/DLP), tighten service account scopes, and validate incident playbooks for **extortion + leak response**.
- **ICS advisories awareness (if applicable to facilities/DC):** CISA ICS advisories (Schneider/Siemens/Festo/Delta) — confirm whether any are in your environment (data centers, building management); isolate and schedule vendor patches if present.
